reason: Title directly indicates this is about subunit configuration of heteromeric cone CNG channels. CNGA3 and CNGB3 (cone cyclic nucleotide-gated channel subunits) are core targets in the gene_or_topic list, and CNGA1 (rod subunit) is studied by comparison. Directly relevant to achromatopsia and cone dystrophy genetics.

Full abstract confirms a detailed mechanistic study of rod phototransduction, cGMP-gated channel physiology, and light adaptation in mammalian vs amphibian rods. Directly relevant to Visual physiology and to CNGA1 (the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel whose gating is central to the cGMP mechanisms described).

Abstract describes a GUCY2D (retGC1) knockout mouse with cone-specific dystrophy. GUCY2D, GUCA1A, and GUCA1B are all in the gene_or_topic list and are directly studied or mechanistically implicated. The cGMP produced by GUCY2D gates CNGA1 channels, and SLC24A1 mediates calcium extrusion in the same outer-segment signaling cascade.

Abstract explicitly measures signal amplification and visual pigment phosphorylation rates in purified rod and cone fractions. GRK1 (rhodopsin kinase) is the enzyme responsible for visual pigment phosphorylation, making this paper directly relevant to the GRK1 gene target. CNGA1 is downstream in the same phototransduction cascade.

Abstract studies pharmacogenomics of steroid-induced ocular hypertension and its relationship to high-tension glaucoma. MYOC (myocilin / GLC1A) is a canonical glaucoma gene and the paper explicitly studies the pathogenetic link to high-tension glaucomas where MYOC is implicated. COL8A2 corneal structural variants may also contribute to aqueous outflow resistance.
Title is 'Macular Dystrophy of the Cornea', which is precisely the disease caused by CHST6 mutations (macular corneal dystrophy / MCDC1). This is a direct disease-gene match.

ARID1B mutations cause Coffin-Siris syndrome. This case series documents optic nerve hypoplasia and dysplasia in Coffin-Siris patients, directly characterising the ophthalmic manifestations of ARID1B haploinsufficiency. Squarely within the ophthalmogenetics scope.

Abstract is a comprehensive review of Ca2+ homeostasis in photoreceptors. CNGA1 (rod CNG channel, main route of Ca2+ entry in the outer segment) and SLC24A1 / NCKX1 (the rod Na+/Ca2+-K+ exchanger responsible for Ca2+ extrusion) are foundational to this review. ACO2 is mentioned in the context of inner-segment metabolism and Ca2+ regulation.

CRYAB (alphaB-crystallin / HSPB5) is a lens crystallin with significant expression in cornea. A review of gene sharing between lens and cornea is directly mechanistically relevant to CRYAB biology, and is also relevant to the Outer coat anatomical topic covering corneal and lens structures.

CDH23 and PCDH15 are the two proteins forming the tip-link in inner ear hair cells, and both cause Usher syndrome (USH1D and USH1F respectively) with associated retinitis pigmentosa. This single-molecule study directly characterises the molecular mechanics and Ca2+ sensitivity of the CDH23-PCDH15 adhesion bond, providing fundamental mechanistic insight into these Usher syndrome genes.

CHST6 encodes carbohydrate sulfotransferase 6, which catalyses sulfation of keratan sulfate glycosaminoglycans in the corneal stroma. A review of sulfotransferases in glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis is directly mechanistically relevant to CHST6 function and to the pathogenesis of macular corneal dystrophy.

Abstract studies mGluR6 (GRM6) in retinal ON-bipolar signaling and explicitly shows mislocalization of TRPM1, Bassoon, and ELFN2 in GRM6-ablated organoids. NYX (nyctalopin) is a GPI-anchored protein essential for mGluR6 signaling at the OPL synapse and is in the same signaling complex; CACNA1F (Cav1.4) mediates depolarisation at the same synapse. Both genes cause CSNB and are directly tied to the circuit studied here.

The paper studies TMEM67 mutations in a large-animal model of Meckel syndrome. The gene_or_topic is CC2D2A, which causes MKS6 (a different Meckel locus) and Joubert syndrome. While TMEM67 and CC2D2A are both transition-zone ciliopathy proteins and produce overlapping syndromes, this paper investigates TMEM67 exclusively and does not study CC2D2A. For a gene-indexed ophthalmogenetics library, a paper about a distinct gene modelling a related but separate disease is correctly excluded under CC2D2A.

Abstract directly studies peripapillary RNFL thickness by SD-OCT in a cohort of choroideremia patients. CHM mutations are the sole cause of choroideremia, making this a direct clinical characterisation of the CHM disease phenotype.

Title indicates this is a linkage analysis paper for choroideremia using closely mapped DNA markers. Choroideremia is caused by CHM mutations; early linkage mapping papers established the CHM locus and are foundational to the gene's clinical literature.

Abstract describes AAV-Foxo1 gene therapy tested in a Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy mouse model. COL8A2 mutations cause FECD1 (early-onset Fuchs dystrophy). A paper developing and validating therapeutic strategies specifically for FECD disease models is relevant to the COL8A2 gene entry.

Abstract explicitly reviews COL4A1/COL4A2-associated microangiopathy as a distinct entity within hereditary cerebral small vessel disease, covering clinical and radiological features. COL4A1 mutations also cause ophthalmic disease (retinal artery tortuosity, cataract, Axenfeld-Rieger-like anomalies); a detailed review of the full disease spectrum provides necessary clinical context for the gene. The paper does not need to be exclusively ophthalmic to be useful under COL4A1 in an ophthalmogenetics library.

Abstract is a retrospective study of a multigene bleeding/coagulation panel in patients with bleeding disorder of unknown cause or cerebrovascular events. COL4A1 appears as an incidental pathogenic finding in a subset of CVE patients, but the paper has no ophthalmic content and its scientific focus is haematology and coagulopathy. The connection to COL4A1 ophthalmic manifestations (the basis for its inclusion in this library) is too indirect to justify inclusion.

Abstract directly studies genetic prediction of progression to endothelial keratoplasty in Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy, combining CTG18.1 expansion status with a FECD-specific polygenic risk score. COL8A2 mutations cause FECD1; this paper characterises the genetic architecture and clinical progression of the same disease, directly relevant to the COL8A2 gene entry.

GAS6 is the primary ligand for MERTK, activating it on RPE cells to mediate photoreceptor outer-segment phagocytosis. Gamma-carboxylation is required for GAS6 to bind phosphatidylserine exposed on shed outer-segment membranes and trigger MERTK signalling. A paper elucidating gamma-carboxylation's role in GAS6 anti-apoptotic and receptor-activating function is directly mechanistically relevant to MERTK biology and to understanding retinitis pigmentosa caused by MERTK loss-of-function.
